sentences.text:
Author: R. Raghunandan Rao
Bench: R. Raghunandan Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice R. Raghunandan Rao
 Crl.P.No.9458 of 2022
Order:

The petitioners are accused in Crime No.412 of 2017 dated 24.11.2017 of Macherla Urban Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 273 read with Section 34 IPC on the ground that the petitioner was caught storing tobacco and tobacco packets.
After investigation the police have filed a charge sheet before the Junior Civil Judge, Sattenapalli, who took cognizance of the case in S.T.C.No.29 of 2018.
2. The cases are being booked against persons, who are found to be either storing or transporting tobacco or tobacco products in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

Persons, who are facing such cases,
have been approaching this Court for relief.

3. In Crl.P.No.5421 of 2019 and batch dated 18.12.2019, a learned Single Judge of this Court had held that tobacco does not fall within the definition of "food" and as such, registration of Crime under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is not permissible.

4. In W.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch dated 27.08.2018, a learned Single Judge of this Court had held that the police would not have jurisdiction to initiate or investigate into any offences punishable under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The learned Single Judge had also held that transport or storage of tobacco and tobacco 2 RRR,J products would not constitute an offence punishable under Sections 270 to 273 IPC.
5.

In view of the aforesaid findings, which are being consistently followed by this Court, this Criminal Petition is allowed quashing S.T.C.No.29 of 2018 on the file of the Junior Civil Judge,
Sattenapalli against the petitioner, with a direction to return the seized tobacco and tobacco products.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

R. RAGHUNANDAN RAO, J.
29th November, 2022 Js.
